[BugFix][KV Transfer] Allocate unique AscendStore save event IDs (#22621)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Use the full UUIDv4 value as a Python integer for each AscendStore save
event ID. Generate a fresh UUID if its full value is already tracked.
Worker completions release the matching KV blocks after all workers
acknowledge the save.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Save event IDs are internal to AscendStore.

### How was this patch tested?

- Three focused scheduler tests passed on Python 3.12 with vLLM main
`c410543d9f`. They cover repeated full-value collisions, distinct
128-bit IDs with the same prefix, and block release after worker
acknowledgements.
- On eight Ascend 950DT devices with Qwen4Exp W8A8, TP8, and
non-layerwise MemCache, four cold requests and four cache replays
succeeded. All five tracked save events used 128-bit integers and
returned from the workers with matching IDs. Each replay restored 4,096
external cache tokens and generated the same token as its cold request.
- Ruff lint, Ruff format, spelling checks, and `git diff --check` passed
for the changed files. Local `bash format.sh ci` timed out while
initializing the actionlint environment.

The TTFT measurements below compare the earlier 32-bit and 64-bit
allocator variants against the main-branch counter.

#### Qwen4Exp non-layerwise TTFT versus the main-branch counter

Ran Qwen4Exp W8A8 on 8 Ascend 950DT devices with TP8 and MemCache. Each
cold request had 4,097 input tokens and generated one token. The
baseline is the main-branch incrementing `next_event_id` allocator. The
comparisons used separate Ascend 950DT hosts. Each row uses the counter
baseline measured in the same server under the same request conditions.

| Paired comparison | Request concurrency | Cold requests per arm |
Baseline TTFT P50 (ms) | Candidate TTFT P50 (ms) | TTFT P50 change vs.
baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main counter → 64-bit UUID | 4 | 12 | 730.9 | 746.0 | +2.1% |
| Main counter → 32-bit UUID prefix | 4 | 32 | 737.5 | 736.3 | −0.16% |

The 64-bit comparison completed three paired batches in the same server.
ID allocation P50 was 0.40 µs for the counter and 8.90 µs for the 64-bit
UUID. End-to-end P50 was 731.0 ms and 746.1 ms, respectively.

The 32-bit comparison completed 8 paired four-request batches per arm.
ID allocation P50 was 0.45 µs for the counter and 9.85 µs for the 32-bit
prefix. End-to-end P50 was 737.6 ms and 736.4 ms, respectively. Both
arms completed all 40 tracked save events with zero retries. All 64
replays restored 4,096 tokens per request from MemCache and produced the
same output token as the corresponding cold request.

In a separate verification with 16 serial non-layerwise requests per
UUID variant, the 32-bit prefix measured P50 values of 9.93 µs for ID
allocation, 371.6 ms for TTFT and 371.8 ms end to end. The 64-bit
variant in that run measured 10.55 µs, 377.5 ms and 377.6 ms,
respectively. Both variants completed all 16 tracked save events. The
32-bit collision-check segment had a P50 of 0.28 µs, with zero retries
observed.

The separate layerwise run completed 16 serial requests with a TTFT P50
of 425.9 ms and an end-to-end P50 of 426.0 ms. This path had zero
tracker calls. Replay probes in both modes restored 4,096 tokens from
MemCache and produced the same output token as the original request.

#### Qwen4Exp 128K cold-input TTFT

Ran Qwen4Exp W8A8 on eight Ascend 950DT devices with TP8, non-layerwise
AscendStore, and MemCache. All three allocators ran in the same engine.
Each allocator handled one batch of four concurrent cold requests, with
131,072 input tokens and one output token per request.

change vs. counter |

| Main-branch counter | 15.19 / 28.92 / 42.64 / 56.19 | 35.78 | Baseline
|

commits.message: [BugFix] Fix missing AscendStore CPU KV events (#22514) ### What this PR does / why we need it? Blockwise AscendStore saves assign different blocks to different workers. Intersecting every worker's CPU KV events drops a block that its own writers have fully stored. This PR publishes a logical block when every rank that writes its keys has reported, and leaves other blocks' writers out of that quorum. A block is ready when `count * group_tp_replication_factor >= num_workers`. The factor is per cache group: `put_step * pcp_size` for ordinary attention, `pcp_size` for DCP and align-state, and `1` for KVPP and sharded Mamba. PP stages stay in the report count because they store different layers of the same block. Reports that arrive on a later step stay in the counter. A worker with KV events enabled still submits an empty batch, so a rank that has not finished still counts toward the quorum. - Publish prepared, complete block ranges after successful PUTs. For partially successful batches, preserve events for logical blocks whose PP-expanded physical keys all succeeded, then follow the existing transfer failure path. - Tag events with `group_idx` so each cache group uses its own replication factor. - Preserve effective cache-group block sizes, token spans, TP block assignment and global parent hashes. - Keep direct PUT exception propagation to the existing outer request handler. ### Testing Result ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. AscendStore CPU KV events include blocks stored by the workers that own them. A block is published once every rank that writes that block has stored it, including when those stores finish on different steps. No new configuration or environment variables. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/22514.yaml`. ### How was this patch tested? - `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_ascend_store_connector.py tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_kv_transfer.py --confcutdir=tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store` passed **101 tests and 77 subtests**. The new cases cover a block published when its own writers finish, a block held until every key writer reports, and per-group replication factors. - Hardware/E2E/performance: **CI testing only**. NPU correctness and performance of the current revision have not been measured locally. --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: empty batches, duplicate events, block/token spans, partial grains, and quorums completed on a later step. - [x] **Regression test**: blocks owned by a subset of workers are published once their writers report; a block that still needs another key writer is held; successful blocks retain events after partial PUT failure. - [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: PUT exceptions, unsuccessful batches and malformed result lengths. - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: assertions check events, hashes, tokens, group indexes and drain behavior. - [ ] **Performance impact**: NPU and distributed validation pending. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15 --------- Signed-off-by: lvvgang <50510955+lvvgang@users.noreply.github.com> Signed-off-by: lvvgang Signed-off-by: ganglv Co-authored-by: Cursor Co-authored-by: ganglv

[Feature] Unify PCP and PP arguments in the external DP launcher (#22747)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The external DP example only accepts TP, so deployments that also use
PCP or PP need their own launcher and template conventions. Add
`--pcp-size` and `--pp-size`, pass TP/PCP/PP together as template
arguments 7/8/9, and allocate `TP × PCP × PP` devices per local DP rank.

The launcher also supports a custom template and validates local rank
ranges before starting processes. It checks every local rank with poll()
every 0.1 seconds; any nonzero exit raises an error even while an
earlier rank is still running. That error, or other Python exceptions
including KeyboardInterrupt from Ctrl+C, triggers best-effort cleanup in
a try/except block: send SIGTERM to every recorded rank process group,
wait for the shells, and re-raise the original exception. SIGTERM sent
to the launcher raises SystemExit and enters the same cleanup path,
exiting with status 0 after cleanup completes. There is no shutdown
timeout or force-kill fallback. Descendants must respond to SIGTERM
themselves; interruption before Popen returns or during cleanup can
still leave processes running. The README documents the fixed argument
order, node-local device allocation, and a combined PCP/PP example.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. PCP and PP can be configured together, with defaults of 1 resolved
by the Python launcher. The launcher always supplies all nine template
arguments; direct shell-template calls must supply PCP and PP explicitly
(append `1 1` to old seven-argument calls). Custom templates using
argument 8 for PP must move PP to argument 9.

`--template` (alias `--script`) selects a template. DCP remains
configured in the shell template and does not multiply device
allocation.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests/ut/examples -p
test_launch_online_dp.py -v`: all 13 tests passed on Windows with Git
Bash. A mocked SIGTERM registration test invokes the registered handler
during monitoring and checks that every recorded group is signalled and
each shell is waited for. Regression coverage checks that a second
rank's nonzero exit (including signal termination) is detected and
cleanup is signalled before waiting on a still-running first rank.
Success requires all ranks to exit with zero status. Other coverage
includes parallel sizes/argument forwarding, invalid inputs, partial
spawn failure, KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit while monitoring, and
signalling already-exited process groups. Process-group operations in
cleanup unit tests are mocked.
- Removed the POSIX signal integration test after it timed out in both
CPU CI variants. Real SIGINT-to-descendant cleanup is no longer covered
by this suite; removing the test does not establish that the underlying
timeout is fixed.
- Focused mypy 1.11.1 checks using Linux platform definitions for Python
3.10, 3.11 and 3.12, plus Ruff lint/format, passed after the removal.
- A real CLI smoke check used two temporary shell workers that each
required both ranks to be running before exiting; both completed
successfully, verifying concurrent startup and command-line argument
parsing.
- The actual shell template was executed with a stub `vllm` function to
verify the forwarded flags and launcher-supplied defaults of 1 and
explicit PCP/PP values. `bash -n
examples/external_online_dp/run_dp_template.sh` also passed.
- Focused repository checks for the changed files: Ruff lint/format,
Codespell, Typos, Markdownlint, ShellCheck, filenames, Python package
initialization, forbidden imports, boolean context managers, logger
usage, long functions, symbolic meta kernels, and a staged Gitleaks
scan. Hooks requiring `/bin/bash` or `python3` were invoked with Git
Bash or Python on Windows.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed.
- `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but did not complete: Actionlint's
Go environment bootstrap stalled and was stopped. Full repository lint
remains for CI.
- NPU validation: **CI testing only**. No NPU inference, multi-node
execution, or performance results are claimed; model/backend support for
the selected parallel combination still applies.

Revert "[CI] Verify accuracy against the lower bound only by default (#22679)" (#22956)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Reverts #22679 ("[CI] Verify accuracy against the lower bound only by
default").

The `ge` mode as merged verifies `acc >= baseline`, which drops
`threshold` from the lower-bound check. That is stricter than the old
`range` mode on the lower side and starts failing cases that used to
pass inside the tolerance band - e.g. `qwen_3_6_27b_w8a8_A3` GPQA in
nightly run
[45143473938](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45143473938):
measured 82.32 vs baseline 84.34 / threshold 5 failed under `ge`, while
the old range check (79.34 <= 82.32 <= 89.34) passed.

The intended semantics (threshold relaxes the lower bound only, upper
bound never enforced) needs a follow-up fix; reverting first to unblock
tonight's nightly runs, since there is no time to validate a fix before
the window.

Note: this revert restores the original behavior where an accuracy
result above `baseline + threshold` fails the case (e.g. the motivating
MiniMax gsm8k 100.0 vs [93, 97] case). That trade-off is accepted for
now; the follow-up PR (#22954) re-lands the lower-bound-only semantics

[Performance] Migrate A5 FP8 indexer to V2 and reuse metadata across layers (#22720)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A5 FP8 C8 indexing currently uses the older QLI interface in each layer.
This change uses CANN V2 and prepares batch metadata once per compatible
indexer cache group during metadata build, so all layers in the group
consume the same result.

- Scope the V2 C8 path to FP8 E4M3 query/key cache (`quant_mode=1`) with
FP32 weights. Remove the added INT8 mode-2 dispatch and test cases.
Unsupported query/key dtypes are rejected before launching the V2
operator.
- Refresh query boundaries, sequence lengths and metadata on every
build. Keep their device addresses stable for FULL graph replay; equal
shapes or addresses do not imply reusable values.
- Isolate buffers using the existing slot-mapping storage key for
separately prepared draft steps.
- Honor configured top-k and retain the inline producer fallback for
direct adaptor calls without prepared metadata.

The producer runs on the current stream. This PR does not add a separate
metadata stream or change the existing sharded-DCP path. A3 INT8 support
is unchanged. C4 is a separate follow-up in #22789.

The FP32 conversion applies to runtime indexer weights produced by
`wk_weights_proj(hidden_states)`, not checkpoint parameters. QLI
metadata configuration, buffers and prepared/inline lookup now live in
`indexer.py` alongside the existing indexer metadata. The separate
`qli_metadata.py` module has been removed. The adaptor uses method-local
imports and type-checking-only annotations to avoid a runtime circular
import.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: A5 FP8 C8 sparse-attention indexing uses CANN V2 and avoids
repeated metadata preparation across compatible layers. No new
configuration switch is introduced. A performance release-note fragment
is included.

The measured comparison includes both the V2 migration and metadata
reuse; the entire difference cannot be attributed to reuse alone.

[BugFix][Attention] Keep SFA draft cache formats consistent with owner specs (#22761)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix the SFA mixed-cache-format inconsistency exposed by the owner-spec
migration in #21370. With target INT8 and draft auto/BF16, spec
construction now uses the layer implementation's dtype, while packed
MRV2 reshape still uses the target-global dtype. Interpreting a BF16
allocation as INT8 produces the twofold element-count startup failure.

Keep the correction local:

- Derive SFA C8/TurboQuant flags from the current layer's cache dtype,
keeping execution and owner-spec construction consistent.
- Reshape packed storage using `kv_cache_spec.dtype`, matching
allocation.
- Add three focused reshape cases covering BF16 draft storage (split and
packed) under an INT8 target, plus an unchanged INT8 control. Update one
existing fixture for the removed dtype-conversion import.

The final diff changes two production files and two test files. The
existing NoPE forward fixture now selects its cache dtype consistently
with its C8 parameter. A5 NoPE reader selection, CANN metadata capacity,
sparse-index handling, and padded-page behavior are outside this fix and
retain their base behavior. No release-note fragment is included.

### Validation

- All **233 tests** in `tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` pass on
the final scoped patch in the remote runtime matching base
`c64ace678d12d5a48671d929c76f723f8158876c`.
- Earlier A3 NPU regression uses the same retained production changes:
two-layer GLM-MoE-DSA dummy-weight fixture, TP1/eager, target INT8 and
explicit draft auto. Baseline reproduces the twofold reshape failure;
the fix completes startup and two eight-token requests, with 14 draft
calls / 14 draft tokens. The removed NoPE reader change is A5-only and
inactive in this A3 case.
- A3 runtime: November 18 CANN 9.3.0 nightly, vLLM
`4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`, vLLM-Ascend
`405617bae227fe5b097ff163efaa60bb7f22c698` plus merged #22108
(`575bafa3f`) to preserve the target configuration during draft loading.
The retained correction was adapted to that older image's source
context.

inheriting INT8 in this vLLM version) completes startup and generation.
This distinguishes the mixed-dtype regression from the default
inherited-dtype case.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.

supplied full P/D topology (P: PP2/PCP16; D: TP2/DP16), full-weight

the opt-in deep review round:

- Reviewer applies the `ai-review` label → agent produces grounded
findings (file:line + rule ID + MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX/NIT)
- Multi-round: developer replies with `@ai-review`; new pushes
auto-revoke `ai-review-passed` and re-review incrementally
- Termination: pass verdict (zero MUST-FIX), per-push round cap (5),
reviewer stop (`/ai-review-stop` or label removal), waiting-human for
design decisions, whole-PR budget (15 rounds)

channel as the doc-translate job); the agent command stays repo-variable

[CI] Right-size CPU runners for lightweight control-plane jobs (#22476)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Most control-plane CI jobs — test selection, matrix setup, benchmark
artifact merging, release packaging, and slash-command handling — spend
their run time on GitHub API calls and file I/O rather than CPU. Running
them on 8- or 4-core self-hosted runners wastes capacity that
compilation, unit-test, and pre-commit jobs actually need. This PR
right-sizes those jobs across three steps, keeping run logic unchanged
except for runner labels and the dispatch consolidation:
1. Downsize CPU runners for lightweight jobs
- 8-core → 2-core: nightly/weekly setup-vars and
merge-benchmark-artifacts, select-all-tests, upload-merged-new-tests
(release code packaging), and the a3/a3-560t setup steps
- 8-core → 4-core: doc translation, full-test selection
- 4-core → 2-core: PR command handlers (/cancel, /rerun, /run, /e2e,
/revert, /cherry-pick), fork coverage comment, upstream tag resolution,
doctest planning, multi-arch image manifest merge jobs (manifest push
only, no compilation), and the profiling plan step
Jobs that genuinely need their cores stay unchanged: pre-commit with
mypy and its cache warm-up (8-core), the cpu-ut partition running
tests/ut (8-core), csrc cache builds and profile trace parsing
(16-core), and docker builds (4-core).
2. Consolidate /nightly dispatch jobs into one matrix job — the ten
dispatch-* jobs become a single matrix job whose legs are composed by
authorize, so only selected targets start a runner (2-core,
max-parallel: 2). Run links travel via dispatch-link-* artifacts, and a
noop leg preserves the previous all-skip behavior while still letting
post-links report the command result.
3. Move pure I/O bot jobs to 1-core runners — gate comment/refresh,
issue triage, merge-conflict check, PR close, e2e result reporting,
refresh-ci-gate relay, recipe preview comments, matrix/setup and
parse-trigger steps, stale management, and slash-command dispatch now
run on linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk.
New runner labels (linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk, linux-aarch64-cpu-2) are
registered in .github/actionlint.yaml so the CI lint hook passes.

No. This is a CI/infrastructure-only change; runtime and user-facing
behavior are unaffected.

[BugFix][CI] Fix silent checkout failure when nightly dispatches with a branch ref (#22903)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Manually dispatched multi-node nightlies die silently when
`vllm_ascend_ref` is a branch name (e.g. the workflow default `main`).

In `checkout_src()` the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` and
resolves the ref against PR refs:

```bash
PR_REF=$(git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/*/head' | grep "^${VLLM_ASCEND_REF}" | awk '{print $2}' | head -1)
```

When the ref is `main`, `grep` matches nothing in the `refs/pull/*/head`
list, exits 1, and `pipefail` + `set -e` terminate the whole script
immediately after `git clone --recurse-submodules` finishes - with no
error output. Any workflow_dispatch run with `request_id` set (making
`is_pr_test=true`, so `checkout_src` is entered) and the default ref
fails in Stream logs within ~3.5 minutes; every other matrix job in the
same run is skipped.

Evidence (run
[45109329614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45109329614),
dispatched with `vllm_ascend_ref=main`): both
`MiniMax-M3-w8a8-PP-prefix-PD` and `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w4a8-PD-MRV2`
jobs died 2s after the googletest submodule checkout (04:04:49 ->
04:04:51) with `run.sh exited with code 1`, before installing
dependencies or launching any test. No container/infra failure involved
- pods were ready and the clone succeeded.

The `/nightly` command path is unaffected because it dispatches with the
PR head SHA, which grep does match - which is why this latent bug
(introduced by #17848) went unnoticed for scheduled nightlies: they do
not set `request_id` and never enter `checkout_src`.

Fix: append `|| true` so the no-match case becomes an empty `PR_REF`
that falls through to the intended `else` branch (`git checkout main`).
Behavior is unchanged for PR-head SHA refs.

## Related issues

None.

## Test cases passed

- Local reproduction with the extracted pipeline: ref=`main` now yields
an empty `PR_REF` (script survives, falls to branch checkout);
ref=`<sha>` still resolves the matching PR ref.
- `bash -n` syntax check passes on the modified script.

[Performance] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel on Ascend (#21196)

## Description

Port of vLLM #58737 to vllm-ascend.

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s "align" branch takes the last `1 +
num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request. As PyTorch
ops this expands to **seven eager kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)`
tensor** - one element per op at one-request decode - so the cost is
launch overhead, not work. Both Ascend call sites (the GDN attention
metadata builder, run by every Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-Next GDN model each step,
and the GLM RecoverSSM metadata builder) are host-side builders
executing **every step, outside any captured graph**, at any batch size.

The upstream kernel cannot be inherited: vLLM gates it with `if not
block_table.is_cuda`, so NPU always falls back to the seven-op
expression **regardless of the vLLM version**. This PR ships the same
kernel for triton-ascend (NPU-only) and swaps the two call sites.
Equivalence vs the expression was probed bit-exact (8/8 shapes) before
implementation; the outputs are integer block IDs (exact-compare
category), so model-level outputs are unchanged by construction.

## Performance

### 910B probe (triton-ascend 3.6.0, per call)

Device ~370 -> ~215 us (**-42%**), host ~247 -> ~121 us (**-51%**); flat
across 1..512 rows - the win is per-launch, per-step.

### E2E on 910B (Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8, MTP5, TP4)

Arms = base tree vs this PR, alternating with cold restarts. Concurrency
1, five independent pairs, zero flips, B faster in all: ITL **-0.112 /
-0.168 / -0.245 ms (-0.7 / -1.0 / -1.4%)**; aisbench TPOT 17.3 -> 17.1
ms, E2E latency -1.0%. Concurrency 8: mean -0.3 .. -1.5%. The -0.112 ms
c1 delta reproduces exactly on an older stack (D05-17U); UT gate 89/89
on the bench NPU; zero failed requests across all rounds.

### Op-level A/B on 910C (both call sites)

A3 single node; arms = `main` (`3e9e1869a`) vs same tree + this patch;
`--profiler-config` torch profiler (CANN `ascend_pt`), per-kernel device
time aggregated from the rank-0 profile. Kernel counts are exact
multiples of the decode step count, so the op-level comparison is
deterministic.

*Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 - default config (TP4, no spec decode, prefix caching
on -> `align`); the GDN build calls the helper exactly 3x per decode
step, 10 launches per call:*

| | baseline (7-op expression) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| kernel launches / decode step | 30 | 3 (**-90%**) |
| family device time, 1022-step window | ~59.8 ms | 3.92 ms (**-93.4%**)
|
| kernel mean time | ~1.9 us | **1.28 us** |
| E2E ITL, 1 req x 1024 tok | 17.093 ms | 16.952 ms (**-0.141 ms /
-0.83%**) |

*GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 - `--use-replayssm --mamba-backend triton` (TP8,
MTP3), the only config selecting call site 2; RecoverSSM rebuilds 3x per
step:*

| | baseline | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| kernel launches / decode step | ~21 | 3 (**-86%**) |
| family device time, 273-step window | ~16.3 ms | 1.04 ms (**-94%**) |
| E2E ITL | 36.657 ms | 36.503 ms (**-0.154 ms / -0.42%**) |

Net decode-step saving is ~0.14 ms on both models (device ~55 us + host
~85 us from 27 / 18 removed launches), fully accounting for the measured
ITL deltas within ~3%. The absolute per-step saving is
batch-size-independent (fixed 3 builder calls/step, ~1.3 us kernel), so
the relative gain peaks at low concurrency. Scoping: under the V2
runner, default GLM serving (no `--use-replayssm`) leaves both call
sites dormant - the host build is bypassed by the in-graph
fused-metadata path (verified: no A/B difference); GLM numbers above are
RecoverSSM-specific, Qwen numbers need nothing beyond default prefix
caching.

### Load-bearing details kept from upstream

- `block_table_stride_0: tl.int64` - without it `req_idx * stride`
computes in i32 and wraps past 2^31 elements; the `torch.gather` it
replaces indexes in 64-bit.
- `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` on all three pointers - callers pass
row-sliced views (`block_table[:num_reqs]`); without it a misaligned
slice JIT-recompiles mid-step. Verified on triton-ascend 3.6.0.
- `n_out` / `block_size` are session-constant and alignment
specialization is suppressed, so the kernel compiles exactly once per
process; no variants remain, so JIT warmup registration does not apply.

## What's Changed

- new `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/align_block_table.py`: kernel
(verbatim port incl. both annotations) + `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`
wrapper mirroring upstream's contract (`none` passthrough, num_reqs
derived from the block table, asserted equal to seq_lens rows).
NPU-only.
- `ops/gdn_attn_builder.py`: import swap; the `[:num_reqs]` slice is now
unconditional (the Ascend wrapper asserts row equality on all vLLM
versions; the old version-gated slice would trip the assert on 0.32.0).
- `models/glm5next/recoverssm_metadata.py`: import swap.
- tests: `tests/ut/ops/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` keeps the `none`
passthrough + shared builders; on-device equivalence moved to
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`;
align-mode cases of the pre-existing builder UTs
(`test_gdn_attn_builder.py`, `test_glm5next_recoverssm_metadata.py`)
gated on NPU availability.

## Test

`tests/ut` runs on CPU runners, so it covers only the CPU-reachable
behavior; the on-device matrix (request counts, block sizes, speculative
depths, non-contiguous block_table, row-sliced views, seq_len-0 clamp,
empty batch; `rtol=0, atol=0`) lives in the e2e nightly test and passed
**89/89 on 910B** before the reorganization.

Possible follow-up (out of scope): generalize the upstream `is_cuda`
gate so device-triton backends inherit the fused path directly.

[BugFix] Honor per-layer SwiGLU limits in Ascend MoE (#22405)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Ling routed experts need to apply each layer's configured SwiGLU gate
limit after SiLU. This PR adapts the upstream fix to Ascend. [vLLM
#65088](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65088)

- Select `swiglustep` for Ling routed layers with a configured limit on
`v0.33.0`. The factory patch is scoped to Ling and that release. The
upstream model already selects the activation at `c410543d9`, so the
patch can be removed when Ascend drops support for `v0.33.0`.
- Resolve `SWIGLUSTEP` limits in the shared MoE input. `None` and `0.0`
use the default limit of `7.0`. Positive limits come from the executing
layer and are forwarded to the regular MoE MLP and W8A8 MXFP8 mode 3.
- Fall back to regular MoE when the target model or MTP draft configures
per-layer SwiGLU limits. This covers local `dispatch_ffn_combine` and
CANN MegaMoe, whose fused paths bypass the corrected MLP. The fallback
preserves the requested shared-expert overlap and clears the derived
MegaMoe and shared-expert fusion flags after the existing mode checks.

verify that `enable_fused_mc2=2` keeps MegaMoe enabled for an eligible
configuration without per-layer limits. Use
`EXPECTED_DEFAULT_SWIGLUSTEP_LIMIT = 7.0` for both default-limit
expectations in the runtime arguments test.

Fixes #22404.

Yes. Ling routed experts with a configured limit apply the gate clamp
after SiLU. `SWIGLUSTEP` uses `7.0` for an unset or zero limit and

[BugFix][GLM] Use current PCP batch span for embedding exchange (#22357)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22356.

GLM-5.3-Flash MRV2 embedding preparation runs before ForwardContext. The
runner already publishes the current PCP-common padded token count
through an optional model hook, but both GLM model wrappers omit that
hook. The vocabulary embedding therefore falls back to its static token
capacity. In the reported profile, rank0 padded 2000 IDs to 16384;
8-rank all-gather expanded these to 131072 positions, producing a 1 GiB
BF16 embedding intermediate.

Forward `set_embedding_num_tokens_padded` through the multimodal wrapper
and causal language model to the existing vocabulary embedding setter.
Skip PP stages represented by `PPMissingLayer`. This reuses the existing
PCP communication plan and runner-provided common length, including any
required padding; it does not independently choose each rank's valid
token count.

**Scope: target preparation vs. MTP drafter.** This PR fixes target-side
MRV2 embedding preparation before `ForwardContext`; it does not add a
drafter span hook or claim MTP correctness or performance validation.

Code inspection against this PR and vLLM `ba15685` distinguishes the GLM
MTP path from the affected target preparation: `Glm5NextMTP` does not
declare `supports_multimodal_embeddings`, so the [drafter capability
check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py#L284)
leaves `supports_mm_inputs=False`. Consequently, the multi-module
drafter keeps `inputs_embeds=None` and skips the external embedding
lookup in `_prepare_inputs`. GLM MTP instead performs lookup inside
model forward under `ForwardContext`, where PCP exchange uses the
current input row count even if the saved span is `None`. Embedding
ownership is checkpoint-dependent: an equal target embedding can be
shared; a distinct draft embedding, or a local copy when the target PP
stage has none, is retained. Neither ownership branch alone establishes
a capacity-fallback issue. This is a source-level assessment, not an MTP
hardware result. Future external multimodal embedding support in the GLM
drafter would require checking common-span publication before any lookup
outside `ForwardContext`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-5.3-Flash PCP embedding preparation uses the current batch's
common padded length instead of padding to the configured capacity when
the runner publishes that length. This removes unnecessary embedding
rows and collective payload for small batches. No new configuration is
required.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU validation used Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, and the
repository's verified vLLM main source
`ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe`, with the main-version
selector (`VLLM_VERSION=0.33.1.dev0`). All runs used an isolated source
snapshot.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_VERSION=0.33.1.dev0 python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_embedding_padding.py \
  tests/ut/ops/test_vocab_parallel_embedding.py \
  tests/ut/worker/v2/test_pcp_multimodal_embedding_padding.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_pp.py
```

Result: **43 passed**. The new regression test keeps the real runner,
GLM wrappers, embedding lookup, mask, cropping, and multimodal merge on
CPU, replacing collectives and external encoder results. It covers both
PCP ranks, unequal valid lengths, graph/alignment padding, shrinking
batches, idle ranks, empty batches, and PP stages without an embedding.

Regression verification: replacing only the model implementation with
unpatched main makes all 6 new cases fail. The 4 data-path cases detect
an all-gather input of 16384 elements instead of the current span of 4;
the 2 PP cases detect the missing model hook. Restoring the patch passes
all cases.

Formatting and lint: all enabled checks passed with
`SKIP=actionlint,markdownlint,shellcheck,gitleaks-offline-scan bash
format.sh ci`, including Ruff lint/format, codespell, typos,
clang-format, and repository Python checks. The unmodified command was
attempted but environment setup was blocked by the container's HTTPS
certificate errors. Offline Python hook dependencies were supplied
through an authenticated download on the client.
Actionlint/Markdown/shell hooks were skipped because this container
lacks Go, Node/npm, and ShellCheck; secret scanning is left to CI. No
workflow, Markdown, or shell source files are changed by this PR. Full
unskipped lint and secret scanning remain required in CI.

NPU validation: an isolated 8-rank HCCL regression/benchmark passed on
Ascend910 hardware with PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu` with the NPU extension
`torch_npu 2.10.0.post7`. The run uses the actual
runner-to-GLM-wrapper-to-vocabulary-embedding path with synthetic,
exactly checkable BF16 weights; it is not whole-model throughput or
model-quality evidence. All ranks matched the expected embeddings bit
for bit, including unequal valid lengths, shrinking batches, an idle
rank, and an empty batch. The baseline removes only the two added model
hooks; both modes use the same libraries and source image (vllm-ascend
`df793dcdee875537fce5741ccfec7be457d3724e`, vLLM
`4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`) with this PR's 9-line model
change applied.

For 2000 tokens/rank, hidden size 4096, capacity 16384, 3 warmups and 10
repetitions:

| Metric | Baseline | Patched | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Intermediate shape per rank | [131072, 4096] | [16000, 4096] | 8.19×
smaller |
| Text: maximum of per-rank median wall latency | 17.449 ms | 3.095 ms |
5.64× faster |
| Multimodal wrapper: maximum of per-rank median wall latency | 17.313
ms | 2.800 ms | 6.18× faster |
| Maximum peak allocated memory during the isolated benchmark | 1434.45
MiB | 421.10 MiB | 70.6% lower |

The multimodal-wrapper measurement exercises embedding preparation, not
a real image encoder. These are single-session subflow measurements, not
an end-to-end speedup claim. Full-layer real-weight validation also
completed on the same source image and checkpoint
`GLM-5.3-Flash-W8A8-1010-V1`, using TP=1, PCP=8, DP=2, EP, eager
execution, ordinary KDA, BF16 KV/indexer caches,
`max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `max_num_seqs=16`, and
`max_model_len=262144`. Both uninstrumented baseline and patched servers
returned HTTP 200 with non-empty outputs for text, image, and a request
containing exactly 131072 prompt tokens and 16 generated tokens. This is
one long request, not a concurrency-16 stress test. Initial text/image
requests were capped at 32 generated tokens and ended in reasoning text;
a subsequent paired diagnostic allowed 256 tokens and completed with
answers `4` and `红色` respectively. This is a functional smoke check, not
a benchmark-suite accuracy evaluation.

Real-request rank-0 kernel traces confirm the embedding output shape
changed from `[131072,4096]` (1 GiB BF16) to `[16384,4096]` (128 MiB
BF16); the current local batch in these traces has 2048 rows/rank. The
observed Gather durations were 4694.080 us before and 198.220/199.880 us
after. These are individual profile samples, not a statistically
controlled operator benchmark. The initial 128K HTTP timings were 39.832
s before and 27.036 s after; they are diagnostic only because
warmup/cache state and profiler overhead differ. Some trace memory
records were incomplete, so no whole-model peak-memory claim is made.

**Output-equivalence qualification:** initial whole-model 128K generated
token IDs differed between baseline and patched runs. Four additional
identical patched requests with `X-data-parallel-rank` fixed to 0/0/1/1
also differed within each route despite temperature=0 and seed=1024.
This prevents a strict generated-token equality sign-off; the downstream
cause has not been isolated. To verify the changed component directly, a
temporary diagnostic in the isolated container ran both exchange lengths
on the same real loaded embedding weights and input tokens before model

[Performance][KV Offload] Delayed batch D2H for sparse KV offload on Model Runner V2 (#20289)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes the sparse KV offload path on Model Runner V2 with two
changes:

**1. Delayed block-wise async D2H pipeline** — replaces the per-layer
synchronous device-to-host KV copies with a batch pipeline that overlaps
the forward pass:
-
`vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`
— the pipeline core: request-level plan freezing (`plan_d2h_requests`),
all-layer descriptor expansion, async launch on a dedicated stream
(`launch_d2h`), and next-iteration settlement with a TP completion
collective (`retire_d2h`); slot generations guard async-window reuse
races
- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` — iteration hooks: retire at
the head of `execute_model` (before state updates / slot reuse),
source-ready recording at the end of `sample_tokens` (past the last KV
writer)
- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_states/default.py` — plan freeze + launch
right after attention-metadata build (copy overlaps the upcoming
forward); publishes settled stable prefixes to attention geometry
- `vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/scheduler.py`
(+ `worker.py`, `protocol.py`) — finished requests keep their resident
rows until every referencing batch retires (delayed-free coordination)

**2. Re-enabled prolog_v3/mlapo fused preprocessing under offload** —
previously disabled because the CANN fused operator only writes paged
caches:
- `vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py` — on decode-only steps the
fused operator's `kv_cache`/`slot_mapping` parameters are redirected to
the resident buffers (`_get_current_layer_resident_cache_tensors`
reshapes them into the paged layout), so the operator writes the
circular tail without modification; the attention geometry now follows
runner-owned, rejection-corrected stable prefixes

This improves performance by overlapping D2H copy overhead with the
forward pass — **TPOT −13.3%, ITL −10.8%, output throughput +15%**
versus the synchronous path (see Performance below).

### Performance

Cross-host PD disaggregation (TP16 prefill + DP16×TP2 decode, MTP3),
versus the synchronous per-layer D2H baseline:

Total throughput (tok/s) |

| Delayed batch D2H | 21.2 (−6.2%) | 71.7 (−5.7%) | 1388 (+6.0%) | 23612
(+5.9%) |
| + prolog_v3/mlapo re-enabled (total, this PR) | **19.6 (−13.3%)** |

failures.

[CI] Skip unowned empty __init__.py files in the CODEOWNERS gate (#22887)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Lists the currently unowned empty `__init__.py` files as `SKIP(owner)`
entries in CODEOWNERS, instead of extending the gate script.

Background: the ci-gate checkout is sparse, so the zero-byte exemption
in `check-coverage` (`os.path.getsize`) cannot see files outside
`.github/` — empty `__init__.py` files without a direct owner show up as
unowned warnings in CI even though a full local checkout exempts them.
Today there are 6 (verified against the live gate log, job
137533549237): `vllm_ascend/attention/__init__.py`,
`vllm_ascend/model_executor/__init__.py`,
`vllm_ascend/models/layer/__init__.py`,
`vllm_ascend/models/layer/attention/__init__.py`,
`vllm_ascend/worker/__init__.py`, `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/__init__.py`.

`SKIP(owner)` is exactly the existing "deliberately unowned" mechanism:
the files are exempt from the coverage warning and need no owner
approval, with zero script changes. Empty `__init__.py` files carry no
behavior, so nothing to own. (This also silences their entries in the
comment bot's "Unclaimed modules touched" section.) A new unowned empty
file would need a new line — non-blocking warning noise in the meantime,
acceptable maintenance.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI-only: 6 false "no CODEOWNERS owner" warnings for empty
`__init__.py` files disappear from the gate output. No release note
fragment (dev tooling, invisible to wheel/Docker users).

## How was this patch tested?

- Simulated the CI condition (exemption disabled) against current
CODEOWNERS: warnings drop 118 → 112, exactly the 6 empty files removed,
all non-empty unowned files still reported.
- `check-coverage` on a full checkout: PASSED, 5075 files, 112 unclaimed
warnings (unchanged).
- Unit tests: 56 pass (`test_codeowner_gate.py`, `--noconftest`).
- Real gate behavior: CI testing only.

[Feature][HiSparse] Enable HiSparse on HDK 25.5.1 with MemFabric (#22600)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#22062 enables native AIV access to CPU KV storage on Ascend A2/A3. The
native registration path relies on `aclrtHostMemMapCapabilities`
supporting AIV Host mapping, available with HDK 26.1 or newer. Many A3
deployments still use HDK 25.5.1. On that stack, the capability query
returns `207000` and HiSparse fails to start.

When a `HiSparseConnector` explicitly sets `"transfer_backend":
"memfabric"`, allocate the private per-rank Host pool with MemFabric
AccOffload in LOCAL mode and use its device virtual address for AIV
refill. The adapter keeps Core's existing backing and registration
contract and releases its arena after Core drains device work. MemFabric
1.3.0 uses its process-local allocator. MemFabric 1.3.1 provides a
dedicated allocator for each arena.

The same option is read from a `HiSparseConnector` inside
`MultiConnector`. The adapter provides LOCAL Host allocation on the
existing Host-pool contract. In the HiSparse P/D design in #22109,
`MooncakeConnectorV2` selects its transport independently and the P/D
manager owns SHARED backing. When integrating the branches, the P/D
manager can select the explicit LOCAL allocator for local HiSparse and
keep its separate SHARED ownership and lifetime rules. This preserves
the Host-pool contract for future P/D integration. The A3 validation
covers LOCAL allocation and connector selection. End-to-end P/D
transport qualification remains with #22109.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On A3 with HDK 25.5.1, users can start HiSparse with the following
KV transfer configuration. The serving environment needs the A3
MemFabric AccOffload extension. When it is missing, build it after
sourcing CANN with `mfcli kernel install --soc-version A3`.

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":8,"transfer_backend":"memfabric"}}'
```

Omitting the option keeps native ACL Host registration as the default.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Focused checks.** Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Twelve
selected Host-pool tests passed on the A3 runtime with each SDK,
MemFabric 1.3.0 and 1.3.1. Tests cover direct and nested connector
selection, initialization-config fallback, ACL default, address offsets,
empty DVA rollback, and allocator shutdown.
- **Repository lint.** Ruff, codespell, typos, Markdown lint, and the
Python policy hooks passed. The full lint run could not bootstrap
actionlint because of dependency download failures. ShellCheck and
offline gitleaks require local binaries and are deferred to CI.
- **A3 hardware.** With the candidate Host-pool code, both SDK versions
passed native AIV refill with byte and LRU checks, cross-stream ACL
Graph replay, and asynchronous D2H with 16 and 17 copy descriptors. The
test closed and recreated the arena in the same process.

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_hisparse_foundation_cpu.py \
```

[BugFix][WeightTransfer] Fix DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision reload weight and add ipc e2e test for V4 Vision (#19328)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision reload after level-2 sleep and add a TP2
NPU IPC regression using the shared weight-transfer framework from
#20535.

#### The fixes

1. **Preserve weightless normalization state.** Register the existing
`weight` tensor as a nonpersistent buffer directly in
`AscendRMSNorm.__init__` when `has_weight=False`, preserving its object
identity. Learned weights remain parameters. This lets Worker buffer
backup/restoration and module device conversion manage weightless
normalization state across models; the DeepSeek-specific traversal
helper and call are removed.
2. **Read current image-marker parameters.** Build the sentinel table
from the current `image_start`, `image_pad`, `image_newline` and
`image_end` parameters instead of retaining a detached copy that becomes
stale after weight updates.

3. **Match upstream profiling inputs.** Accept optional `input_ids` in
`AscendModelState.dummy_inputs_embeds()` and delegate calls carrying IDs
to the upstream implementation. The existing idle-batch embedding TP
path remains in use when no IDs are supplied. This fixes Vision startup
profiling with the paired vLLM main interface.

Production changes are in `vllm_ascend/ops/layernorm.py`,
`vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/vl_model.py` and
`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_states/default.py`; the model-specific
buffer-registration changes in `model.py` have been removed.

The PR uses main's shared weight-transfer framework. It keeps #21384's
deletion of the local `mm_preprocess.py` and imports the upstream
`vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.mm_preprocess` implementation.
Processor-interface fixes already in main are not reintroduced as local
overrides.

- The Vision IPC entry point reuses the shared TP2 transaction. The BF16
reduced case uses **4 text layers, 2 vision layers, 8 routed experts, 3
hash layers and no MTP**; its only model-specific extra server argument
is `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`.
- `checkpoint_adapters.py` supplies vision, aligner, marker and
Vision-only `bias_vl` parameters missing from HF text-model enumeration;
persistent HF router buffers are enumerated once by the shared source.
IPC/HCCL construct sources through main's `make_weight_source()`; Vision
uses the default `FixedRandomWeightSource`, main's shared fixed-seed
sampler and its existing visual-parameter builder.
- Reference and live-update servers both use `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with
`cudagraph_capture_sizes: [1]`, matching main. Two text requests and one
image request are compared with independent startup loading, including
exact output and token logprobs.
- Marker UTs verify that all four parameters affect the next embedding
call. Main's upstream-preprocessor tests are retained.

with `InputProcessingContext`: one/two images, with/without text
truncation, each overlapping twice with renderer tokenization through a
shared local fast tokenizer. Image tensors, token IDs, hashes and
placeholder ranges/masks must match serial baselines. A synchronized
guard rejects accidental image-path re-tokenization.

Yes. DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision retains weightless normalization state and
uses updated image-marker parameters through the existing level-2
sleep/wake and NPU IPC update lifecycle. No new public API, CLI option
or production environment variable is added.

Coverage uses a complete generated payload. This PR does not establish
arbitrary omitted-parameter preservation. No IPC retention override,
global reload skip-list change, dedicated retention runner or Vision
HCCL entry point is added. Sentinel construction stacks/casts the
current parameters; no performance improvement is claimed.

[BugFix][Ops] Retire eager packaged MLA stream uses on Ascend A5 (#22592)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The packaged CannBotDSL MLA call records the query and attention output
on the submission stream. In eager execution these records can delay
buffer reuse and increase memory pressure. After submitting the kernel,
record and wait on a device event on that stream, then retire the
recorded uses of `q` and `attn_out`. The cleanup is gated to eager
execution.

[Attention][Feature] Enable PCP decode request sharding for GLM-5.3-Flash (#22131)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3-Flash currently replicates decode requests across PCP ranks.
This PR uses the upstream Model Runner V2 decode ownership policy when
PCP > 1 and DCP = 1, assigning each request, including speculative
target verification, to one rank round-robin within the batch.

KDA gathers inputs in global request order so every rank advances its
recurrent-state shard, including when a request changes owner or a rank
has no live requests. It returns local outputs through packed
ReduceScatter where supported, or the existing projection and local
selection. KDA still processes the global request sequence internally;
state updates are not owner-only.

KPool and compressor-tail cache writes use global metadata while queries
stay local. Sharded decode capture and replay use matching padded global
metadata extents. GLM native GDN and RecoverSSM builders size their
capture buffers for that global extent using a private config view,
without changing runner capture sizes or generic GDN/Kimi RecoverSSM
behavior. Persistent permutations live in GLM builders, preserve the
shared PCP context, and skip unused copies for replicated pure decode.

A known SFA short-prefill/speculative-lookahead issue can still trigger
a collective mismatch on this branch.

This PR retains main's existing joint TP/PCP Mamba validation in
AscendStore.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With Model Runner V2, GLM-5.3-Flash decode requests are
automatically distributed across PCP ranks when
`--prefill-context-parallel-size` is greater than 1 and
`--decode-context-parallel-size` is 1. PCP = 1 and DCP > 1 retain their
decode policy. No new switch is introduced. KDA state and KPool cache
writes stay synchronized across PCP ranks.

The context-parallel guide documents the behavior.
`release_notes/fragments/22131.yaml` covers decode sharding and graph
capture support.

[Feature] A2/A3 fold Q/K L2 normalization into the FLA NPU GDN prefill kernel (#21678)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Cut the work the A2/A3 GDN chunked prefill adaptor does around the FLA
NPU GDN kernel:
let the kernel normalize q/k itself, and stop materializing copies that
only existed to
satisfy the old call signature.

- Drop the two standalone l2norm_fwd launches on q and k and pass
use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True instead.
- Replace the unconditional transpose(1,2).contiguous() on q/k/v with a
contiguity check: reuse the head-first view when the transpose is
already contiguous (layout=BNSD), otherwise pass the sequence-major
contiguous tensors (layout=BSND).
- Switch the kernel call to state_v_first=True and remove
initial_state.transpose(-1,-2) on both input and output; the keep_meta
scatter now runs on a clone of the caller's full state.

Scope: only BaseDeviceAdaptor.fla_gdn_prefill in
vllm_ascend/device/device_op.py.

Why this is worth it: GDN prefill is performance-sensitive on A2/A3 (see
flash-linear-attention-npu issue 656). Per prefill layer the adaptor
previously paid two extra kernel launches and several full-size tensor
copies for no functional gain. No numerical change is expected: the
in-kernel L2 norm computes the same q/k normalization that the removed
l2norm_fwd calls did.

Existing test updated:
tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_layout.py::test_head_first_l2norm_fallback_accepts_multiple_heads
asserted the previous contract (external l2norm_fwd plus unconditional
BNSD). It now checks the
in-kernel normalization flag and the contiguity-driven BNSD/BSND choice
instead.

#### External prerequisite

This change depends on fla_npu work that is now available in the 26.10.0
release branch.

vllm-ascend currently pairs with fla_npu 26.9.1 (mkdocs.yml,
release_fla_npu_version), which predates that
work. Until the pairing is bumped to a 26.10.0-based build, the
optimized prefill path this patch relies on
is not what ships with a stock wheel.

This PR should therefore land together with, or after, the fla_npu
26.10.0 pairing bump.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

NO

### How was this patch tested?

- New CPU regression tests: tests/ut/device/test_fla_gdn_prefill.py (7
cases) verifies the kernel argument
contract, the BNSD/BSND layout selection, the untransposed recurrent
state, the keep_meta scatter, and the
  g/beta dtype casting. A recording stand-in replaces the fused kernel.

[BugFix] Revert the CODEOWNERS empty-file blob-size check that hangs ci-gate (#22868)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Reverts ac7c428adb (#22662) to unhang the ci-gate "CODEOWNERS coverage
check" step, which has been running for hours on every gate run since
that change landed (e.g. run
[45114337341](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45114337341/job/137512029083);
multiple PRs affected, 360-minute timeout never reached).

Root cause: #22662 assumed actions/checkout still fetches every blob
under `sparse-checkout`. It does not — checkout applies
`--filter=blob:none` automatically whenever `sparse-checkout` is set
([git-source-provider.ts](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/main/src/git-source-provider.ts)),
so blobs outside `.github/` are absent. `git ls-tree -r --long HEAD`
must report each blob's size and triggers a lazy promisor fetch per
missing blob (~4k round trips). Reproduced locally with a `blob:none`
partial clone: 30 s and <20% of entries listed; with a full fetch the
same command takes 0.03 s.

Why revert instead of a targeted fix: dropping the sparse checkout (full
depth-1 checkout, ~200 MiB transfer) also fixes it, but the revert is
the minimal safe step — the only regression is that empty `__init__.py`
files are again reported as non-blocking `::warning` coverage noise in
CI, which we lived with before #22662. A partial-clone-safe exemption
can be designed separately.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI-only; unblocks the merge gate for all open PRs whose coverage
check is stuck.

## How was this patch tested?

- Root cause reproduced locally (see above); revert restores the
pre-#22662 code path that ran in CI for days without hanging.
- CI testing only for the real gate job — after merge, the stuck gate
jobs need cancel + re-run.

[Performance] Tile DCP rank reduction on A2/A3 (#19555)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DCP A2A combines one attention-output contribution and its log-sum-exp
(LSE) from each context-parallel rank, plus an optional local FIA
contribution. For BF16, each received row contains D output values and
four packed LSE values; receive layout is [DCP ranks, local heads,
tokens, D+4], and result layout is [tokens, local heads, D]. The scalar
kernel visits ranks serially for each row. This PR adds an A2/A3
rank-tiled path that computes the same LSE-weighted result across ranks
and feature tiles. This PR contains only the DCP/Triton optimization;
MoERunner.forward override removal is independently reviewed in #20248.
The DCP branch was rebased through main `6924c0889` and remains
independent of the MoE PR. The interfaces, layouts and A5 batched
pack/combine implementation from #17387 are retained. No HCCL collective
or four-lane LSE wire-format change.

The earlier DCP16/D512/T>=16 dispatch described measured shapes, not a
general crossover. This revision selects by rank reduction, feature
tiling and total work instead:

- BF16, head scatter, a local FIA contribution and contiguous local
features;
- `4 <= R <= 16`, `Rtile = next_power_of_2(R)`;
- `F = min(128, next_power_of_2(D), 2048 // Rtile)`;
- `R >= 2 * ceil(D / F)` to amortize repeated LSE loads;
- `T * H >= max(ceil(4 * vector_cores / R), ceil(vector_cores / ceil(D /
F)))` to provide enough work.

The work thresholds and rank range were selected from A3 measurements;
cross-device speedups are not established. Rank and feature tails are
masked. Feature-strided local inputs retain the scalar fallback because
their measured tiling regression remains relevant. A5 uses the main
batched/scalar paths; the rank-tiled kernel is disabled on A5.
Unsupported types, layouts, small work and other rank counts retain
existing paths. Related tracking: #19663.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower eligible DCP merge overhead without new configuration or host
transfers. The shared dispatch can be reached from decode and
chunked-prefill callers; measurements in this PR cover Kimi-K3 decode
only, and no prefill speedup is claimed. Parallel FP32 summation changes
the reduction order and can cross BF16 rounding boundaries compared with
the scalar FMA loop. It is not claimed bitwise equivalent to the old
reduction.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Current-main operator validation (2026-10-28)

A3, original `nightly-main-a3-openeuler-20261021174845` image, torch
2.10 / torch_npu 2.10.post4, private CANN 9.2 overlay, one device in an
isolated two-NPU task; no model service. Benchmark code loads this PR's
Triton kernels and current-main scalar source. The operator harness uses
the existing vLLM `a98247ab` runtime; final source tests use main's
verified vLLM `544f182d`.

The matrix completed 72 synthetic cases. Its first 64 span R=2/4/8/16,
D=96/256/512/1024, T=1/4/16/64 and local H=4. An initial occupancy-only
rule exposed regressions (DCP4/D512-T64 1.174x, DCP4/D1024-T64 1.913x,
DCP8/D1024-T64 1.347x). The final work-based rule excludes these
regions.

Twenty timed cases remain selected by the final rule, with
candidate/baseline ratios **0.237–0.860**. Each case used ABBA graph
captures **within one process**, five warmups and three samples of 100
replays per block. Both arms execute on the same A3 device; a
dispatch-only device-type override selects main's scalar kernel for the
baseline. The final selector is a strict subset of the initial measured
selector; tiled kernel math is unchanged. Samples are not independent
end-to-end A/B pairs.

| R | D | T | Local H | Scalar µs | Tiled µs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 256 | 16 | 4 | 25.216 | 20.244 |

| 16 | 512 | 4 | 4 | 25.644 | 21.585 |

Eight additional DCP32 small-head cases completed, but the current-main

Final-source validation of the earlier A3 implementation: 28 device

The following measurements belong to the earlier joint MoE + DCP

[CI] Verify accuracy against the lower bound only by default (#22679)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Flips the default accuracy verification mode from `range` (baseline ±
threshold) to `ge` (lower bound only), per the team review decision that
accuracy above the upper bound should no longer fail a case.

Motivating incidents where a *good* result was rejected by the range
check:

- `MiniMax-M3-BF16-A3` nightly (run 42635289613): gsm8k-lite measured
100.0 vs baseline 95 / threshold 2 -> failed because 100 > 97.
- `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w8a8-PD-MRV2`: GPQA measured 93.43 vs baseline 88
/ threshold 5 -> failed because 93.43 > 93.

With `ge` as the default, both cases pass (results only improve), while
regressions below the baseline still fail.

Behavior:
- `verify_mode` defaults to `ge`: accuracy must be >= `baseline`. Values
above `baseline + threshold` pass but log an info-level re-baselining
hint so owners can update stale baselines.
- `verify_mode: range` remains available for cases that intentionally
need an upper bound (e.g. detecting response collapse); set it
explicitly in the case YAML.

## Related issues

Team review decision (2026-11-20): accuracy exceeding the upper bound
will no longer be verified.

## Test cases passed

- Syntax check on `tools/aisbench.py` passes; logic self-check confirms:
100.0 vs [93, 97] now passes with a re-baseline hint, 91.0 still fails,
93.43 vs [83, 93] now passes.
- All 97 existing accuracy-bearing case YAMLs are unaffected except that
upper-bound-only failures disappear; the one existing explicit
`verify_mode: "ge"` case (310P textvqa) behaves identically.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

comment on a PR is driven by a single, structured source and only runs
when the PR actually changes source code.

**`coverage_comment.py` (rewritten)**

- Added `--input-json` (a slipcover `coverage.json`) alongside the

commits.message:
[Feature][MoE] Fuse the shared expert into the A3 MegaMoe operator for W8A8 (enable_fused_mc2=3) (#22207)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`enable_fused_mc2=3` (MegaMoe shared-expert fusion) was gated on the A5
MXFP
contract only, so A3 (`910_93`) W8A8 INT8 deployments always fell back
to the
separate shared-expert forward. A3 runs the shared expert inside the
same
MegaMoe operator for the INT layouts, and this PR enables that path.

Changes:

1. `vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py`: new capability
`CANN_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION_INT` added to the A3 capability set.
The
   MXFP variant (`CANN_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION`) stays A5-only.
2.
`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py::_validate_megamoe_shared_expert_fusion`:
accept the flag when the platform advertises either the FP (MXFP) or the
INT
   fusion capability; the error message now names both platforms.
3. `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/shared_experts.py`:
- `_setup_megamoe_shared_fusion` branches on the MXFP vs INT capability.
The
     INT path allows routed `QuantType.W8A8` / `W4A8`.
- `_collect_megamoe_shared_weight` builds the INT8 shared payload with
the
routed layout, i.e. logical `(in, out)`: `(hidden, 2*inter)` for `w1`
and
`(inter, hidden)` for `w2`, cast to `FRACTAL_NZ`. The A5 `(out, in)`
     transpose is applied only for the non-int8 dtypes.
- The INT8 per-channel dequant scale is packed as one fp32 inside a
`uint64`
(`view(torch.int32).to(torch.int64).view(torch.uint64)`) and passed 1-D
ND.
4. `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py`: forward
`shared_weight1_type` / `shared_weight2_type` whenever the shared fusion
advertises a weight type (previously only when it differed from the
routed
   type), so the operator resolves the INT8 shared GMM mode.

### INT8 layout and scale contract

The routed INT8 experts define the contract the shared GMM reuses:

- weight: logical `(in, out)`, `ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ`, one `int8` per
element
(`w1` is `(hidden, 2*inter)`, `w2` is `(inter, hidden)`). No transpose.
- dequant scale: per-channel, one fp32 value carried in a `uint64`,
passed as a
  1-D ND tensor. This matches the A3 epilogue
(`ScaleType = GemmType<uint64_t, VectorLayout>` in `mega_moe_arch22.h`).
A
  bf16 scale is silently reinterpreted by the epilogue and corrupts the
shared-expert output, so the packed default is not optional for
correctness.

### Bring-up A/B switches

Three environment switches are kept while the INT8 shared layout is
still being
cross-checked against CANN versions. They are bring-up aids, not
user-facing
configuration, and the defaults are the validated shape:

- `MEGAMOE_SH_INT8_WEIGHT_LAYOUT` (`nz` default | `nd`)
- `MEGAMOE_SH_INT8_SCALE_LAYOUT` (`col` default | `row` | `exp` |
`col3`, only
  consulted when the scale is not packed)
- `MEGAMOE_SH_INT8_SCALE_DTYPE` (`uint64` default | `bf16`)

The chosen payload shape is logged once per process. Happy to drop them
before
merge if reviewers prefer a fixed layout.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: `enable_fused_mc2=3` now works on A3 with W8A8 / W4A8 quantization,
and the
rejection message on unsupported hardware names the supported platforms.
A
release note fragment is added in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

Measured on a PD-separated deployment of a W8A8 INT8 MoE model on 2 x
8-die
Atlas 800I A3 (`910_93`):

- Accuracy gate: GSM8K 1319 passed.
- Decode TPOT: ~120-131 ms before -> 56-66 ms after.
- E2E throughput: +1.6-1.8x.
- 7 PD performance groups measured (prefill/decode, multiple concurrency
/

Local checks: `python -m py_compile` on the four changed files, plus
`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (all clean).

Unit tests were not added: the path needs a real MegaMoe operator on
NPU, so the
layout/scale contract is verified through the accuracy gate and perf
groups
above rather than a CPU test. Nothing is claimed for hardware other than
A3
W8A8; A5 keeps its existing MXFP behavior.

---

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: not applicable to a

[BugFix][MoE] Share DSpark MegaMoE contexts across CANN buffer APIs (#21727)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 with DSpark and CANN MegaMoE creates separate target and
draft buffers on the same MC2 group. On A5, the second native context

[BugFix] Preserve the DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE cursor during bounded replay (#22420)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

On a single Ascend A5 node serving prefill and decode together,
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GSM8K accuracy rose from **75.22% to 97.38% (+22.16
percentage points)** with this fix. These are three-round means among
completed answers. Counting all scheduled questions, the correct-answer
share rose from **2,905/3,957 (73.41%) to 3,833/3,957 (96.87%)**.

With `fast_moe_cold_start`, each MoE dispatch advances the cursor in the
current forward context. Bounded replay creates a new context with a
cursor of zero, so in the captured Flash runs decoder layers 21–39 used
expert weights from layers 0–18. The fix seeds the replay context with
the outer context's current cursor so the tail continues at the correct
layer.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes incorrect DeepSeek-V4.1 outputs under SWA bounded replay
with speculative decoding disabled. Existing serving configurations can
be retained.

### How was this patch tested?

- **CPU regression:** All eight replay context cases passed in an
isolated local CPU run and failed at the cursor assertion on the
unpatched base. The supplied validation at Ascend `b64139a5` reports 114
focused tests passed on each vLLM ref (`ba15685a` and `v0.33.0`).
- **A5 mixed deployment:** The supplied A/B used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on
16-card Ascend950PR nodes, 200-shot GSM8K, concurrency 512, and 1,319
questions per round. Both arms used the downstream vLLM 0.32 debug

on different physical nodes. Read timeouts were 96 and 21, respectively.
The first baseline round also used a different retry policy. Replay

wrong layers in all nine baseline samples.
- **Disaggregated P/D:** The supplied A5 run also confirmed correct

(97.27%).
- **Local checks:** `bash format.sh ci`, `git diff --check`, Python

commits.message:
[BugFix] Exempt empty files from CODEOWNERS coverage check in CI sparse checkout (#22662)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

The CODEOWNERS gate job checks out only `.github/` (sparse) so a PR
cannot weaken the gate script or CODEOWNERS. `is_contentless_file`
relied on `os.path.getsize`, which raises `OSError` for every file
outside `.github/` in that working tree, so the zero-byte exemption for
empty `__init__.py` broke in CI: unowned empty `__init__.py` files were
reported as coverage warnings again (e.g. run
[44713215032](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44713215032/job/136211945876)).
Locally the exemption still worked (full checkout), which is why it went
unnoticed.

Fix: read blob sizes from the git object store via `git ls-tree -r
--long HEAD`, which works regardless of working-tree sparsity because
`actions/checkout` fetches all blobs even for a sparse checkout. The
working-tree fallback is kept for callers without a git size map, so
partial local checkouts still report missing files as unowned.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI-only: fewer false "file has no CODEOWNERS owner" warnings for
empty `__init__.py` in the gate job. No release note fragment (dev
tooling, invisible to wheel/Docker users).

## How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added: `TestContentlessExemption` in
`.github/workflows/scripts/test_codeowner_gate.py` gains two cases —
sparse working tree exemption via git sizes, and PR-only paths missing
from the base-branch size map still being reported. Full suite: 58
passed locally.
- Manual: `check-coverage` locally exempts 0-byte
`vllm_ascend/attention/__init__.py` via the git size map while 6KB
`vllm_ascend/models/__init__.py` is still reported.
- CI testing only for the NPU side (no hardware involved in this change;
gate job behavior verified by CI).

[Feature] Fuse GatingTopK with EPLB expert mapping (#21587)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With ModelRunnerV2 EPLB, expert selection writes logical expert IDs
before a separate Map kernel reads them and produces physical IDs. This
change adds an optional `expert_replica_routing_table` input to
`moe_gating_top_k_hash`, allowing supported routes to map the final IDs
before they leave on-chip memory.

The router automatically selects fusion on supported A3/A5 hardware for
ungrouped `sqrtsoftplus` routing. It reuses the existing periodic EPLB
table, including the AllGather table when applicable, and skips the
subsequent standalone Map. Weights are computed using logical IDs before
the output IDs are mapped. The router inherits upstream
`_select_experts` unchanged. An internal `_use_gating_top_k_with_map`
switch is resolved once at the first routing call, after EPLB/capture
setup and using the actual hidden size. The existing Ascend mapping hook
only reads this fixed choice; it does not reset or consume per-call
state. `_can_fuse_gating_map` checks eligibility once, while
`_get_gating_map_table` reads the current ordinary/AllGather table on
every nonempty fused call. Missing tables raise instead of returning
unmapped IDs. The original parent-fallback condition is preserved;
eligibility is resolved for the fixed model routing configuration. The
router retains the existing nonempty-input expectation: the reviewed
ModelRunnerV2 target paths skip zero batches or provide dummy/padded
tokens before routing. This PR does not add standalone zero-row TopK
support. Model routing configuration, including logical-ID capture, must
be finalized before the first routing call and remain fixed during
serving; this change does not add a capture setter override or support
runtime reconfiguration. The mapping-hook check can be removed when
upstream provides a backend contract for already-mapped routing results.
The original TopK expert-count checks remain unchanged; there is no
additional 512-expert fusion limit.

Routes with a logical-ID capture callback or unsupported fusion
conditions retain the original flow. The optional table defaults to
`None`, preserving standalone TopK behavior. Python and compiled
operators must come from matching versions.

Scope is GatingTopK+Map only; Dispatch+Record, MegaMoE+Record and the
separate block-FP8 compatibility fix are not included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On supported A3/A5 ModelRunnerV2 EPLB routes, fusion is enabled
automatically and removes a separate expert-mapping operator launch per
MoE layer. No new flag is needed; replica-selection behavior is
unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- **25 CPU tests passed (19 router + 6 factory/patch):** upstream
selection flow, table forwarding, output dtype, no duplicate mapping,
capture configured before routing, unsupported configurations/hardware,
missing-table errors, and ordinary/AllGather table replacement. Tests
also cover one-time initialization for enabled and disabled choices,
kernel failure/retry, parent fallback, supported/unsupported vision
paths, EPLB disabled. Kernel and communication calls are mocked in these
tests; they validate control flow, not NPU execution.
- **20 A3 single-NPU tests passed in 10.00s** using a fresh build of the
kernel source: Ascend 910_9382, CANN 9.2.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post7. These earlier component results cover the unchanged
kernel. The final fixed-switch router refactor was validated by the 25
CPU tests above; NPU and end-to-end router validation have not been
rerun after that refactor.
- Exact physical-ID agreement against both standalone Triton Map and an
independent CPU table lookup; exact weight agreement with the same TopK
operator with Map disabled.
- FP32/FP16/BF16, eager and NPU graph replay, mixed replica counts,
shuffled nonidentity placement, and in-place table updates.
- Representative `(tokens, experts, hash)` cases: `(1, 384, false)`,
`(33, 513, true)`, `(1025, 2048, false)`.
- Real `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` counts and production Record-buffer
increments match CPU expectations for count/cumulative formats,
recording enabled/disabled, repeated accumulation, and a local expert
range. The production AllGather counting helper also matches masked CPU
counts. These are single-device component checks, not distributed
collective validation.
- The single-NPU test lives in
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/`, which is already
included by the A3 and A5 nightly single-card operator jobs. The old
PR-only A3 runner mapping has been removed. The relocation preserves the
test content exactly; Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed. NPU
execution under the new nightly directory was not rerun for this
relocation; the local `bash format.sh ci` attempt could not run because
`pre-commit` is not installed.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. The full local `bash
format.sh ci` attempt was blocked by CRLF shell-script line endings;
full repository CI remains pending.

Reproduction (with matching compiled operators and their environment
sourced):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ut/ops/test_gating_map_router.py -q
python -m pytest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_gating_map_npu.py -q
```

separately.
